prompt: Prepare a decision memo for the founders of a company selling modular thermal-storage units to independent grocery stores. Ten stores in Northern California have paid for 14 units; nine stores have operated them through four months of peak-demand days, eight still use them, and four have ordered a second unit. Installations came through two local energy contractors, but the founders still attend every site survey and solve commissioning problems. A national equipment distributor will place the product in 80 branches if the company commits next week to $4.5 million of inventory and promises 30-day delivery. The current units have been observed only in warm weather; a redesigned compressor from a new supplier will enter the next batch, and the first reliable cold-season data cannot arrive for five months. The board wants weekly signup targets and a nationwide preorder campaign now. Recommend whether to accept the distributor deal and what growth decision should replace it if not.
criteria: Treats acquiring-and-growing-users as primary because one defined segment has paid, operated, and expanded, while identifying the unproven nationwide distributor loop rather than the existence of demand as the decision under review.

Rejects weekly signups or preorders alone as sufficient justification and matches the review cadence to the five-month physical-use and reliability interval, separating the existing warm-weather units from the cold-season and redesigned-supplier cohort.

Chooses the smallest bounded channel intervention, using an additional regional store-and-contractor cohort with manual installation and support, and does not make the $4.5 million inventory commitment until the loop works without hidden founder rescue.

Measures the channel path from contractor or demonstration encounter through order, installed-and-commissioned activation, continued physical use, and second-unit expansion, with source cohorts, support burden, channel cost, supply or reliability confounders, and accountable store effects rather than top-line leads alone.

Sets a dated review with precommitted repair, expand, pause, and stop thresholds for activation, reliability, retained physical use, founder support, channel economics, and inventory exposure; preserves the distributor option with a switch condition and assigns channel evidence to growth, rollout exposure to shipping, manufacturing machinery to engineering, and distributor economics to business-model ownership.
